algorithm: Restart Economics: expected cost per incoming task, with agent spend, verification and a priced outside option (annotated engineer time). Policy ladder: no retry, retry with best attempt budget (K at most 4), retry with a per-attempt iteration cap, schedules by coordinate ascent, a receding-horizon restart rule on three state variables, and cascades across configurations. Exact replay of truncated logged trajectories scores each policy. Break-even is stated in multiples of the median attempt cost.
methodology: Four logged OpenHands runs on each of 500 SWE-bench Verified tasks, 7 configurations, 13,681 attempts. Exact replay by truncating logs, enumeration of the 24 ordered draw selections, 5-fold task-grouped cross-fitting, full-pipeline task bootstrap (1,000 replicates for the primary result, 100 for comparators). Comparators: dollar cutoff, Kitagawa-Tetenov empirical welfare maximization threshold, Luby-Sinclair-Zuckerman universal schedule, first-look rule, sample oracle. Preregistered on OSF before results. A synthetic population checks interval coverage (93 to 99 percent over 120 samples) and the state rule against backward induction.
key_numbers: Automated verifier, $100 an hour: retry cuts expected cost 13.2 to 19.6% for six configurations and 4.3% for GPT-5.2; at $300 an hour 16.4 to 21.0% (GPT-5.2 8.0%). Dollar savings per task at $100 an hour: GPT-5 5.67 [3.42, 8.80], GPT-5.2 1.01 [0.45, 2.16]. The iteration cap adds nothing given retry: break-even 2.14 to 3.83 median attempt costs ($1.74 to $7.08 an hour); margin never distinct from zero on the cost side in any of 532 cells; best hindsight cap saves at most $0.03 per task. Attempts still running at 100 calls resolve 33 to 55% of the time. Only 11 to 25% of tasks have mixed outcomes. Cross-configuration outcome correlation 0.62 to 0.90. Cascades save 9.2% in point estimate at $100 an hour, interval includes zero. Review at 0.5 of the outside option: no configuration retries, the cap saves $0.75 to $3.56 per task at $100 an hour. The fitted state rule stops 42 to 78% too early and costs 7 to 32% more than the exact optimum on synthetic attempts.
limits: Clean restarts only. One benchmark, one harness (OpenHands CodeActAgent), at most 4 attempts. A configuration is not a model. SWE-bench Verified contamination. The outside option is annotated time, understated for short tasks. The state rule has 8 coefficients; learned monitors are untested. Working paper v0.1, single author, not peer reviewed.
use_for_project: Retry priced by cost per resolved task with the fallback priced; the 2-to-4-full-attempts break-even rule for whether to cap; iteration limits as guards, not levers; replay of logged trajectories for exact policy evaluation (the replay adapter function); cross-fitting with a full-pipeline bootstrap in the eval harness; price review before deciding to run the agent at all.
corrections: none
new_techniques: Restart Economics (cost per incoming task with a priced outside option)
Exact replay of truncated logged trajectories
Break-even in multiples of median attempt cost
Kitagawa-Tetenov empirical welfare maximization threshold rule

algorithm: Gist tokens: insert k gist tokens between prompt and input; mask so later tokens cannot see the prompt; trained by instruction finetuning at no extra cost. Meta-distillation L_G = KL(pLM(y|t,x)||pG(y|G(t),x)).

corrections: 40% FLOPs is vs no caching; vs KV caching the gain is ~0.11%, real benefit is storage.

algorithm: Routing is a linear program. Theorem 1: the optimum is gamma*s_MIN + (1-gamma)*s_MAX at the lambda that meets the budget, found by binary search over lambda. Cascading is sequential routing over supermodels M_1:i (Theorem 2). Cascade routing picks among all supermodels containing the models already run (Theorem 3), with supermodel quality E[max member quality] and cost summed. Lemma 1 prunes negative-marginal-gain models.
methodology: RouterBench 0-shot and 5-shot with 3, 5 and 11 models and Gaussian noise levels Low/Med/High. 5% of the data tunes hyperparameters, 95% evaluates; metric is AUC of the quality-cost curve with bootstrap 2-sigma intervals. Realistic benchmarks: SWE-Bench (10 and 5 agents), Qwen Math+Code, Llama/Gemma/Mistral classification and open-form with logistic-regression quality estimators.
key_numbers: Table 1 0-shot AUC at 11 models Low/Med/High: routing 83.25/74.63/72.67, cascade baseline 84.48/73.64/69.79, cascade ours 84.47/75.10/70.26, cascade routing 87.24/77.57/74.40. Gains up to 8% over cascading and 12% over routing. SWE-Bench: 54.12 vs routing 40.47 (10 models). Realistic noisy estimators: 1.2% mean gain. Runtime 15 ms; Greedy 1.4 ms with 0.5-1.3 point loss.
limits: Gains depend on estimate quality; with poor estimators cascade routing only matches routing. Quality estimators are trained per model and per computed-model history. Up to 2^k supermodels; Normal handles 40 models in 1 s, Max-Depth 3 handles 80. Hyperparameter search is harder for cascades; in 5-shot low-noise cascade ours trails the baseline in two of three cases.
use_for_project: Counts as a model-routing/cascade saving: choose per query among models under a cost budget. Use the realistic 1-14% AUC gains over routing or cascading, not the noise-free RouterBench peak. It gives no savings if only one model tier is available or quality estimates are weak.

Supermodel quality as expected maximum of member qualities, proven submodular (Lemma 6)

algorithm: Observation masking replaces tool observations older than a rolling window of M turns with a placeholder, keeping reasoning and actions (M=10 best in SWE-agent). LLM-Summary summarizes N=21 turns at once, keeping M=10 trailing turns. Hybrid (N=43, M=10) masks first and summarizes only as a deferred last resort.
methodology: SWE-agent on SWE-bench Verified (500), 250-turn limit; five configs (Qwen3-32B with/without thinking, Qwen3-Coder-480B, Gemini 2.5 Flash with/without thinking); 95% bootstrap CIs; OpenHands probe (50 instances); hybrid on Verified-50.
key_numbers: Both strategies cut cost by more than 50% in most configs
Qwen3-Coder: cost $1.29 raw vs $0.61 masked (-52.7%); solve rate 53.4% raw, 54.8% masked, 53.8% summary
Gemini Flash with thinking: solve rate 40.4% raw, 36.4% masked, 31.4% summary (significant drops)
Hybrid 7% cheaper than masking and 11% cheaper than summary, +2.6 pp over raw (Qwen3-Coder, Verified-50)
limits: SWE domain only; fixed non-adaptive triggers; M must be re-tuned per scaffold (M=10 hurt OpenHands, which needed M=58); naive hybrid with N=21 got worse from KV-cache misses and summary overhead.
use_for_project: Rows 11 and 24. Use masking as default, summary as deferred last resort. Account for KV-cache invalidation and summarizer cost (up to 7.2% of instance cost). Tune M per scaffold.
corrections: Earlier record was empty (extraction returned nothing); the full text supplies all numbers above, plus trajectory elongation (summary runs were longer: Gemini Flash 52 turns vs 44 masked, 50 raw) and observations being about 84% of an average turn.
new_techniques: window size M as a per-scaffold hyperparameter

algorithm: Split the document into 128-token chunks, score each by cosine similarity (BGE-large-en-v1.5), take the top-k, then order the selected chunks by their original document position rather than by score (OP-RAG). Answer quality follows an inverted U against the amount of retrieved context.
methodology: InfiniteBench En.QA (351 pairs, F1) and En.MC (224 pairs, accuracy); Llama3.1-8B and 70B generators; baselines: full long context without RAG, SELF-ROUTE, vanilla score-ordered RAG.
key_numbers: En.QA Llama3.1-70B: OP-RAG-16K 44.43 F1; OP-RAG-48K 47.25 F1 vs 34.26 F1 for full 117K context
Vanilla RAG at 128 chunks 38.40 vs OP-RAG 44.43
En.MC: OP-RAG-24K 88.65 vs 71.62 without RAG; vanilla at 192 chunks 81.22
8B peaks near 16K tokens; 70B peaks at 48K (En.QA) and 32K (En.MC)
limits: Long-document QA only; sweet-spot context length varies by model and task; advantage over vanilla RAG is small at around 8 chunks; no limitations section.
use_for_project: Row 37. Retrieve a bounded set instead of stuffing full context, keep retrieved chunks in document order, and tune k per model.
corrections: Earlier '44.43 vs 34.32' mixed numbers: the paper gives 34.32 in the intro and 34.26 in Table 1. It missed 47.25 at 48K, the En.MC results, the model-dependent sweet spot, and the order-preserve vs vanilla gap.

methodology: BFCL categories (simple, multiple, parallel, relevance, live, non-live, multi-turn); xLAM-2-3b/1b, Qwen3-4B/1.7B/0.6B, TinyLlama-1.1B, TinyAgent-1.1B; Gorilla OpenFunctions 2,000 points; DPO on ALFRED only.
key_numbers: xLAM-2-3b-fc-r 65.74% overall, 55.62% multi-turn (Table IV)
Qwen3-4B 62.04% overall
Qwen3-0.6B 45.76% overall, 1.38% multi-turn
TinyLlama and TinyAgent about 19.7% overall, 0% multi-turn

algorithm: Capability instruction = model capability representation + user instruction + Yes/No prompt. The representation is a natural-language aptitude profile from 50 MMLU tasks x 20-shot per candidate. E5-Large encoder, MLP connector, Phi-3-Mini 3.8B; score is P('Yes'). In-batch negatives, two-stage tuning, data refinement. Router never runs candidates.
methodology: 66 open LLMs for training, five zoos plus a multimodal zoo; in-domain MMLU, WinoGrande, ARC-C; out-of-domain BoolQ, TruthfulQA, MRPC, MNLI; 60-model incremental-release simulation.
key_numbers: Table 2 (MMLU/ARC-C/TruthfulQA/mean): Model-SAT 79.86 / 72.53 / 65.12 / 72.50 vs encoder-less Phi-3 74.71 / 70.58 / 61.70 / 68.83
High-performance zoo reaches 85.64 MMLU
Union of 5 small models covers 90% of GPT-4o's correct instructions
A new model needs only 50x20 inferences to onboard
limits: Benchmark-style multiple-choice instructions, not agent traces; requires training; needs an aptitude test per new model; no limitations section.
use_for_project: Row 12. Cheap onboarding of new models via a profile; routing overhead independent of the number of candidates.
corrections: 'State of the art routing' is overstated: the paper only claims better than the best single model and comparable to the 70B in its own zoos. Missed the encoder/connector design, the 60-model incremental setup, the multimodal extension, and that encoder-less variants were weaker.

algorithm: K=4 early-exit MLP heads at evenly spaced layers, trained with KL loss to the main model output; random init beats lm_head copies; entropy is the best confidence metric. Calibrated threshold per head is the smallest confidence whose accuracy against the main model is at least epsilon. DSSD drafts up to 32 tokens with the first head and verifies them in one full pass.
methodology: Pythia 70M to 2.8B, 500K MiniPile examples, epsilon swept 0.5 to 1.0, eight benchmarks; DSSD vs LayerSkip on a 24-config grid, 200-token greedy decoding, V100.
key_numbers: Pythia-2.8B epsilon=0.5: 58.6% speedup, PIQA 0.742 to 0.615; moderate epsilon gives 10-20% speedup
DSSD at epsilon=0.9: 88.8% acceptance vs LayerSkip best 53.6% (1.66x)
DSSD discards 8 tokens vs 128; mean exit layer 13.6 vs 24
Speedup grows with model size
limits: Modest speedup if accuracy must be preserved; only Pythia up to 2.8B; needs model internals; no end-to-end wall-clock for DSSD.
use_for_project: none directly (operator-side inference optimisation, not under a Token Economics user's control).
corrections: Earlier record had speedup unread; the 7.6-58.6% range is now captured with the DSSD contribution, head-initialisation finding and entropy result.
new_techniques: DSSD (draft with early-exit head, verify in one pass)
calibrated exit threshold from held-out accuracy

algorithm: Prompt the LLM to omit a set W of 25 easily inferable function words; a small encoder-decoder or decoder model reconstructs the full text. W is chosen by RoBERTa masked-prediction ranking (cut-off level 5, about 18% tokens saved). Break-even: C_D^o*G >= C_D^i*I + C_R^i*I_R + C_R^o*O_R.
methodology: NaLDA, 44,800 entries over 5 tasks; generators GPT-4o, GPT-4.1/mini, Sonnet 4, Opus 4.1; reconstructors BART, T5, Qwen2.5-0.5B/1.5B fine-tuned on 100K Wikipedia paragraphs; metrics include the new Theta F1.
key_numbers: GPT-4o with T5: 19.41% tokens saved, Theta F1 85.51, cosine 99.99%
Tokens saved: GPT-4.1-mini 22.79%, Sonnet 4 17.83%, Opus 4.1 17.38%
Added instruction costs 169 tokens; break-even answer length about 216 tokens (GPT-4o), about 190 (Sonnet 4)
limits: English only; rewrite/summarize/translate tasks about 5.77% lower; not tested on code, conversation or reasoning models; effect of omission on generation quality untested; needs a trained reconstructor.
use_for_project: Row 36. Only worthwhile for long outputs, with an explicit break-even check. Unsuited to code or agent tool calls.
corrections: Earlier record omitted the break-even condition, the 169-token overhead, the 17-23% variation across models, the code/conversation limitation and the quantified metric decrease.

algorithm: Reward r = -(C + lambda_L*L + lambda_E*1_error + lambda_A*1_abstain): prices of error, latency and abstention. Pick the model or system maximising expected reward, for a standalone LLM, a cascade, or a router with abstention. Cascade error reduction CER = Cov(deferral, small-model error), related to AUARC.
methodology: MATH, 500 questions at levels 1, 3, 5; Llama3.3-70B, Llama3.1-405B, GPT-4.1, o3, DeepSeek-R1, Qwen3-235B, zero-shot CoT; P(True) self-verification deferral tuned on 250 and tested on 250 (level 5); Llama3.1-405B as judge.
key_numbers: Reasoning models cost 10-100x more per query, up to 10x slower, but win once error price exceeds about $0.01 (abstract)
Single Qwen3-235B beats a cascade once error price exceeds $0.10
Llama3.1-405B to Qwen3-235B cascade beats the big model up to error price $10,000 and latency $10/minute
Cost and latency are linear in deferral rate
limits: MATH only; possible contamination; judge model may inflate 405B's self-verification; no separate limitations section.

algorithm: kvtc: one-time per-model calibration computes a PCA basis (randomized SVD, 8 iterations) on 160K-200K tokens with RoPE removed and layers/heads concatenated. methodology: Models Llama 3.1 8B, Llama 3.3 70B, Mistral NeMo 12B, MN-Minitron, Qwen. Benchmarks GSM8K, MMLU, MATH-500, QASPER, Lost-in-the-Middle, RULER-VT. Baselines KIVI, GEAR, H2O, TOVA, xKV, Palu, and vLLM+LMCache for serving. Ablations on window size, calibration data, bit types and PCA vs alternatives.
key_numbers: Llama 3.1 8B at kvtc 64x: GSM8K 57.2 vs 56.8 vanilla, MMLU 60.7 vs 60.5, LITM 90.2 vs 99.4, RULER-VT 95.9 vs 99.8, QASPER 37.8 vs 40.4. Llama 3.3 70B MATH-500: 75.6 vanilla, 73.2 at 8x, 74.4 at 10x, 72.6 at 20x. Latency at BS=8, 8K: compress 379 ms, decompress 267 ms; TTFT 380 ms vs 3098 ms recompute. vLLM+LMCache, 16 clients: TTFT 7.3 s vs 181.6 s.
limits: Storage and transfer only: decoding attends over the decompressed cache, so no GPU memory saving during decode. Needs per-model calibration. Retrieval degrades at 64x (LITM 90.2 on Llama, 59.5 on MN-Minitron). Compress/decompress cost hundreds of ms per batch. Gains depend on long reusable prefixes.
use_for_project: Counts as a prefix/KV-cache reuse technique: it lowers re-prefill cost and TTFT by storing or moving caches about 8-20x smaller with about 1 point quality loss on reasoning. At 64x, retrieval tasks lose quality. Do not credit it with decode-memory savings.
corrections: Earlier record's 'text truncated, read ~40000 of 90.5k chars' is superseded: the full text was read except the references. Its 20x within about 1 point and 64x retrieval degradation claims are consistent with the paper. Unexplained oddity: Table 13 w=128 kvtc64x Llama row equals the vanilla row exactly; flagged, not asserted as error.
new_techniques: RoPE removal before PCA so keys decorrelate across positions
Cross-layer and cross-head concatenation before PCA, motivated by Procrustes alignment
DP bit allocation over types [None,int2,int4,fp8] and block sizes [1,16,64,256,1024]
Calibration PCA basis reused across all compression ratios
Uncompressed 4 FP8 sink tokens plus 128-token recent window
Randomized SVD (Halko, 8 iterations) capped at 10K dims (8K for Qwen)
nvCOMP DEFLATE entropy coding of quantized PCA coefficients

algorithm: Two-tier cascade Mbase -> Mlarge -> human. Verification confidence from surrogate token probability YES/(YES+NO) (also self-verification, consistent self-verification, MC-dropout STP), calibrated by Bayesian logistic regression on 100 samples; posterior mean is confidence, posterior std is uncertainty. Defer if confidence <= phi_base; abstain if uncertainty > xi. Thresholds tuned online by Adam on a soft-masked system risk 1-E[Correct]+lc*E[Cost]+la*P(abstain).
methodology: Qwen-2.5 1.5B->7B (also Llama pairs in appendix) on ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, MMLU, MedQA, MedMCQA; CoT; cost = size*(t_in + rho*t_out) with rho=5; online stream of 1,000 questions, lr 0.05, batch 10, lc=1e-5, la=0.1.
key_numbers: Cascade has lower cumulative regret than either single model on 4 of 5 datasets; MedQA unclear
Verifying with the large model gives better delta-IBC; on ARC2-Easy delta-IBC up to 258.4 +-39.1 with large-model verification vs about -2 to -37 with base
Calibration set size 50-500 samples makes no significant difference
Label flipping in calibration raises regret
limits: Sensitive to cost and abstention weights (trivial solutions); initialisation affects convergence; needs human feedback; MedQA no gain; multiple-choice QA only.

algorithm: Dynamic value-thresholding: add abstention action with reward r_bot; abstain at any token position when estimated value V_t (probability the final answer is correct given the prefix) falls below r_bot. Value estimated by a two-layer MLP probe (~10^4 params) on last-layer hidden states, trained with binary cross-entropy over all non-terminal prefixes of completed traces. Threshold T_alpha is the alpha-quantile on held-out data.
methodology: Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct and Phi-3-mini on GSM8K and OlympiadBench, 5 seeds; baselines Constant Step Probe, self-assessment, LoRA abstention at t=0 and fixed k; also RealToxicityPrompts. Proofs of dominance over no-abstention, fixed-position abstention, and optimality.
key_numbers: OlympiadBench Phi-3 at 90% abstention: 0.64 selective accuracy vs 0.34 best baseline (base 16%)
Qwen OlympiadBench at 90% abstention: 0.91 vs 0.75 best fixed-position baseline (base 43%)
Retains 63-86% of input-only token savings at 10% abstention, 92-95% at 90%
Threshold hits target abstention rate within 1.2 points MAE; zero-shot probe transfer works across datasets
limits: Needs hidden-state access and a trained probe per model; theory assumes oracle value; experiments on math and toxicity only; saves fewer tokens than input-only abstention at low rates.
use_for_project: row 45 (no stop on failure): early termination of doomed reasoning. Needs open-weight hidden states; for API agents only the idea (stop and escalate on predicted failure) transfers.
corrections: Earlier record fine. Add that token savings are a fraction of input-only savings, it needs a trained probe and hidden states, and results are on math reasoning not agents.
new_techniques: mid-generation value probe on hidden states
quantile-threshold calibration for target abstention rate

algorithm: Cost per test = hourly GPU cost x wall time. Hourly cost = depreciation + power + maintenance (about $0.79/h per A800; cloud $2.82-5.64/h). Sweep serving concurrency to find the cheapest setting that still meets throughput (>20 tok/s) and TTFT (<1s) limits.
methodology: WiNEval-3.0, 2,993 medical requests, nine models, 2xA800 80G, swept over concurrency; score vs cost per test set.
key_numbers: WiNGPT-3.5 concurrency 8->48: total time 2034s->774s; 48 optimal. WiNGPT-3.5 76.2 at $0.34 vs Seed-OSS-36B 72.2 at $0.55. Thinking model WiNGPT-3.0 emits 3.44M output tokens vs about 0.35-1.4M for others.
limits: No training cost or capex, hardware-stack dependent, proxy benchmark, no confidence intervals, weak link to API billing.
use_for_project: Reasoning/output-token volume row (about row 45) and tokenizer inefficiency; supports cost = time x rate and an optimal-concurrency zone.
corrections: Earlier record missed that reasoning models cost far more through output volume (4-8x tokens) and the tokenizer effect (Mistral-Small 2.11M input tokens vs about 1.35M, attributed to weaker Chinese tokenization). 48-concurrency figure correct.
new_techniques: cost = wall time x amortised hourly GPU cost

algorithm: Speculative cascades. Drafter q proposes gamma tokens; verifier p scores them in parallel. A token-level deferral rule (Chow, Diff, OPT, or token-specific V1-V3) sets target (1-delta)q + delta*p. GenSpecSample (Algorithm 4) generalizes speculative sampling to that target. Lossy SD is a special case.
methodology: T5 v1.1 small/base/large/XL on WMT EN-DE, XSum, CNN/DM; T in {0,0.1,0.5,1}, gamma in {3,5,7}. Gemma v2 2B drafter with 9B or 27B verifier, few-shot on 8 tasks, 1000 prompts each. Wall-clock latency on TPUv4, batch size 1, 500 examples, 3 trials.
key_numbers: Table 2 (T=1, gamma=5, Small to Large) latency reduction at large-model quality, WMT/XSum/CNNDM: SpecDecode[Lossy] 1.61/1.10/1.57x; SpecCascade[OPT] 1.95/1.17/1.80x; Token 1.85/1.18/1.89x. Best quality at large-model latency, WMT BLEU: Lossy 17.26, OPT 18.33, Token 22.50.
limits: Two-model setup only. Higher total compute than sequential cascades. Plug-in estimators need calibrated models. Objective is local per position. Batch size 1, TPU. Evaluation protocol differs from standard SD. No fairness analysis. Paper claims no new state of the art. OPT weaker on Gemma than T5.
use_for_project: None for API users: needs token-level access to both models' logits inside the serving stack. Provider-side technique only; no billing lever.
corrections: Earlier record said it matches cascade quality at reduced cost; replace with Table 2 numbers. The speedups are against the large model and baselines like Lossy SD, often modest (1.1-1.9x). Earlier black-box inapplicability note is now confirmed by the method.
new_techniques: Diff deferral: defer when max q < max p - alpha, exactly computable because p is scored on every prefix
OPT deferral: threshold max p - alpha*TV(p,q), a plug-in estimate of the optimal rule
Token-specific multiplicative rule V3: p(v) < max p * (1-alpha)
GenSpecSample: speculative sampling for an arbitrary target distribution

algorithm: Adaptive Length Penalty RL. Reward = 1[correct] - beta*N*max(p_solved,1/K), p_solved estimated online from K=16 rollouts per prompt. Easy prompts (high p_solved) get strong length penalty, hard prompts weak. Works with GRPO, RLOO, Reinforce++.
methodology: DeepScaleR-1.5B, 100 steps, batch 512, beta=1e-7. Evaluated on AIME 24+25, MATH-500, OlympiadBench vs L1-Exact, L1-Max, ThinkPrune, R1-Alpha and public checkpoints (not matched training).
key_numbers: About 50% fewer tokens; MATH-500 Pass@1 0.81->0.80 with tokens 2326->646. 40% higher Pass@1 at 1024 budget on easy math. Adaptation ratio 5.35x vs 2.41x base. R1 and QwQ-32B use >10,000 tokens on '2+3'.
limits: Math only; compared against public checkpoints; mixed-difficulty stress test accuracy fell 0.89->0.52.

corrections: Earlier record missed the adaptation-ratio analysis, behaviour analysis (repetition 269->126, backtracking 34.9->13.3) and L1-Max's inverted-U.

algorithm: Layer-wise post-training quantisation minimising ||WX - W^X||^2 using inverse-Hessian updates. All rows quantised in the same column order, lazy batch updates in blocks of 128, Cholesky reformulation with 1% dampening.
methodology: Calibration on 128 C4 segments of 2048 tokens; OPT and BLOOM families; perplexity and per-token latency on A100 and A6000.
key_numbers: OPT-175B quantised in about 4.2 GPU-hours on one A100. 4-bit perplexity 8.34->8.37 vs RTN 10.54. Per-token latency A100 230->71ms (5 GPUs to 1); A6000 589->130ms (8 GPUs to 2).
limits: Speedup is memory-movement driven, weights only (no activation quantisation), kernels target batch size 1.
use_for_project: none (server-side weight compression, not controllable by an API/CLI user).
corrections: The 4.5x A6000 figure compares 2 GPUs with 8, not like-for-like; gains apply to low-batch memory-bound decoding.
new_techniques: lazy block updates and Cholesky inverse

algorithm: Test-Time Speculation: online distillation of the draft model during decoding, one gradient step per round on L = KL(p||q) + lambda*KL(q_t||q); update can run every S rounds on a separate CUDA stream. S=5 is the throughput sweet spot; K>1 steps overfit.
methodology: Eight benchmarks; Qwen3-4B/8B/32B, Qwen3.5-122B, Llama3.1-8B; built on DFlash and EAGLE-3.
key_numbers: Acceptance length up to +72% (+41% avg) vs DFlash; +67% (+34% avg) vs EAGLE-3. Throughput up to 1.71x. Baseline acceptance collapses to about 1.1 beyond roughly 20K tokens; AIME24 gain +15% in first 10K vs +183% at 20-30K tokens.
limits: Needs a backward pass, server-side only, stride trade-off.
use_for_project: none (server-side). Only supports the point that long outputs erode speculative-decoding gains.
corrections: Earlier record conflated baselines: 72%/41% is vs DFlash only. PARD is only a diagnosed baseline, not a target. Missed throughput numbers.
new_techniques: asynchronous draft update on separate stream

algorithm: FLARE length-aware router. Two XGBoost predictors give accuracy p^ and output length L^ from MiniLM-384 query embeddings plus model features. Latency = k_m*L^ + b_m, cost = pi_in*l_in + pi_out*L^. Filter models with p^ >= tau, then pick argmin alpha*T^ + beta*C^.
methodology: Three modes (Acc, Efficient, Balance); KNN retrieval for unseen datasets; new model cold-starts from about 200 requests.
key_numbers: Up to 68% lower latency and 75% lower cost (Efficient mode, 5-20% accuracy sacrifice). FLARE-Acc keeps accuracy with up to 59% latency and 69% cost cut. Latency vs output length Pearson r=0.96. Routing overhead 18.12ms.
limits: Short benchmarks, open models only, three preset modes.
use_for_project: Model-routing row 12: cost is predictable from predicted output length; route to the cheapest model passing an accuracy gate.
corrections: 68%/75% headline is the Efficient mode with accuracy loss. Earlier record missed cold-start method, XGBoost predictors and the length ablation (model-mean length is worse than per-query).

algorithm: Measure tokenisation disparity: tokenise FLORES-200 with the gpt-3.5-turbo tokenizer, average tokens per sentence per language; run tasks to measure prompt+generation cost; correlate cost and utility with Human Development Index.

limits: 2023 gpt-3.5-turbo tokenizer, only 2 models, FLORES translationese, zero-shot costs only.

corrections: none known. Note data is from the 2023 tokenizer; newer tokenizers may differ.

algorithm: Compare long-context (LC) vs RAG with the same LLM (GPT-4o). Filter questions answerable without context; compare 5 retrievers (BM25, Contriever, text-embedding-3-small, Llama-Index Tree/Window, RAPTOR); pick the best; analyse by source and question type.

key_numbers: LC 56.3% correct vs RAG (RAPTOR) 49.0%. LC-only correct 2,287 vs RAG-only 1,294 (about 10% only RAG). RAPTOR best retriever at 38.5% on the retriever-comparison sample.

corrections: Paper contains no token or cost numbers; remove any cost claim attributed to it.

algorithm: CALM per-token early exit. At layer i exit if confidence >= threshold lambda_i (softmax top-2 gap, hidden-state saturation, or trained linear classifier); skipped layers copy state from exit layer; threshold decays with position. Calibrated by Learn-then-Test with Hoeffding-Bentkus p-values to bound textual or risk consistency.
methodology: 8-layer T5 1.1 on CNN/DM, WMT15 EN-FR, open-book SQuAD; 50 trials, 80/20 split; speed on TPUv3.
key_numbers: Oracle exit uses 1.53 layers per token on CNN/DM (potential 5.2x). Calibrated speedup up to about 3x (3.15x on SQuAD at delta=0.1). Copying K/V instead of hidden state drops ROUGE-L to 23.02.
limits: Requires model modification and training, small T5, short outputs gain less, softmax exit can increase FLOPs.
use_for_project: none (server-side architecture). Calibrated risk-bound idea could inform gating a cheaper model.
corrections: none known
new_techniques: calibrated early exit with Learn-then-Test guarantee

algorithm: RouterEval: router as m-way classifier over an input embedding predicting a one-hot or multi-hot best-LLM vector. Splits 8:1:1; easy m in {3,5}, hard m in {10,100,1000}.

algorithm: Compute-optimal test-time scaling: estimate prompt difficulty (base pass@1 from 2048 samples, 5 quantile bins, or predicted via verifier scores); per bin and budget choose the best strategy on a validation fold. Strategies: PRM-guided search (best-of-N, beam, lookahead) and sequential revisions mixed with parallel sampling.
methodology: PaLM 2-S* (Codey) on MATH, 12k train / 500 test; PRM trained with Monte Carlo rollouts; two-fold cross-validation.
key_numbers: Up to 4x less test-time compute than best-of-N (16 vs 64 generations search; 64 vs 256 revisions). Beam search better at low budget and hard questions, best-of-N on easy and high budget. About 38% of correct answers flipped to wrong by naive revision. vs about 14x larger model: test-time compute wins on easy/medium or low inference load only.
limits: Math only, one model family, needs fine-tuned revision and verifier models, difficulty-estimation cost excluded.
use_for_project: Reasoning effort/overuse row 45: allocate effort or sample count by task difficulty; Token Economics can set effort tiers but not train.
corrections: Earlier record omitted that difficulty-estimation cost is excluded from the 4x figure, that fine-tuned models are required, and that gains vanish on the hardest questions and under high inference load.

algorithm: ATLAS benchmark. 3+5 taxonomy (foundational: retrieval, aggregation, reasoning; application: QA, ICL, code, memory, holistic). Length-aware trapezoidal AUC per dimension; ATLAScore is the harmonic mean of three category aggregates; delta-method confidence intervals.
methodology: Nine components, 6,438 instances, 8K-1M geometric length grid, 26 models.
key_numbers: Gemini-3.1-Pro-Preview leads at 128K; Claude-Opus-4.6 leads at 1M (ATLAScore 70.55). 20 of 26 models change rank between 128K and 1M. Mean relative decay 24.3%; Opus-4.6 loses 8.5%, GLM-4.7 non-reasoning 60.5%. GPT-5.2 retrieval 88.21->47.31 at 1M.
limits: English only, holistic at original lengths, model-generated AMemBench transcripts, no summarisation, contamination risk.

corrections: Earlier record correct that it is methodology without cost effect; add the 128K vs 1M ranking reshuffle and capability-specific decay as load-bearing findings.

algorithm: DistillSpec: white-box knowledge distillation of the draft model toward the target before speculative decoding. Draft-generated (on-policy) data is recommended. Divergence (FKL, RKL, JSD, TVD) is a tuned hyperparameter. Acceptance rate is 1 - TV. Optional lossy SD lenience via epsilon.
methodology: GPT-like 234M target and 33M draft on LM1B; T5 v1.1 small to XXL on XSum, CNNDM, WMT, GSM8K; BBH for transfer. 300k steps, batch 32, LR 3e-4, Adafactor. TPUv4, batch 1, 500 examples, 3 runs. Compares SupervisedKD, SeqKD, ImitKD, f-Distill, GKD.
key_numbers: 10-45% speedup over standard SD; 26% average on transfer. Table C.1 examples: XSum T=0 gamma=5 1.43x to 1.62x; CNNDM gamma=7 2.07x to 2.53x; LM1B gamma=3 3.66x to 3.97x. Distilling the target first cuts latency 6.4x on XSum (17.3 to 2.7) and 10.7x on GSM8K (15.0 to 1.4).
limits: Needs target logits and training compute. Task-quality gains and SD-compatibility gains are only weakly correlated. SupervisedKD on fixed data is worst; SeqKD ignores logits. Direct TVD minimisation is not consistently best. Transfer shown only on T5 and BBH. Batch size 1.
use_for_project: None for API users: requires white-box access to the target model. Relevant only to a provider or self-hosted team distilling its own draft.
corrections: Earlier record said 20% speedup and 8x latency. Full text: 10-45% over standard SD (about 20% average on four tasks) and 6.4x on XSum, 10.7x on GSM8K. Earlier record said five tasks; it is LM1B plus four T5 tasks, plus BBH for transfer.

Distill the target first, then DistillSpec the draft (model garden)
